skill.name: git-commit
skill.description: Create conventional Git commits by reviewing diffs, staging selected files, and generating clear commit messages.
skill.summary: Generate conventional commit messages and run safe Git commit workflows.
skill.author: github

security_audit.summary: The skill is a Bash-enabled Git helper that inspects diffs, stages files, and creates commits. Most static findings are Markdown formatting or protective secret warnings, but the Git command blocks are real external command usage that can modify repository state.

remediation.issue: The skill runs Git commands through Bash.
remediation.suggestion: Limit execution to git diff, git status, git add, and git commit, and require user approval before staging or committing.

remediation.issue: The multi-line commit example uses shell command substitution.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer writing the message to a temporary file and using git commit -F to reduce shell quoting and delimiter risks.

remediation.issue: The skill relies on users to avoid secret commits.
remediation.suggestion: Add an explicit staged-file review step for .env files, credential files, private keys, and generated secrets.

content.value_statement: Teams need clear commit history, but writing consistent messages takes time. This skill reviews changes, stages selected files, and creates conventional Git commits.
actual_capabilities: Reviews staged and unstaged git diffs before writing a commit message.
Identifies Conventional Commit type, optional scope, description, body, and footer.
Stages selected files, path patterns, or interactive hunks when requested.
Creates single-line or multi-line git commits with generated messages.
Applies safety rules for secrets, destructive commands, hooks, and force pushes.
limitations: Requires Bash access to run local git commands.
Does not verify that tests pass unless tests are run separately.
Can only commit changes present in the current repository.
Needs user review for logical grouping and sensitive file checks.

use_cases.title: Daily Feature Commits
use_cases.description: Turn finished feature work into a concise conventional commit with an accurate scope and description.

use_cases.title: Review-Ready Fixes
use_cases.description: Prepare focused bug-fix commits that are easier for maintainers to review and trace.

use_cases.title: Structured Release Work
use_cases.description: Create clear commits for build, CI, and release changes with consistent metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Commit Staged Changes
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner workflow for already staged files.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a conventional commit for my staged changes. Explain the selected type and message before committing.

prompt_templates.title: Stage One Commit Group
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my working tree, suggest one logical commit group, stage those files, and create a conventional commit after I confirm.

prompt_templates.title: Split Logical Commits
prompt_templates.prompt: Split these changes into separate logical commits. Propose scopes, stage each group, and commit only the group I approve.

prompt_templates.title: Write Breaking-Change Commit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for API or behavior changes.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this breaking API change, create a multi-line conventional commit with a body and footer, and avoid amending existing commits.

output_examples.input: User asks to commit staged documentation changes.
output_examples.output: The skill reviews the staged diff, selects a documentation type, and creates a concise documentation commit.

output_examples.input: User has mixed test and feature edits.
output: The skill recommends separate commits for test work and feature work.
It stages only the approved group before creating the first commit.

output_examples.output: The skill writes a conventional commit with a breaking-change marker, body, and footer.

best_practices: Review the diff summary before allowing staging or commit creation.
Confirm that no secrets or generated files are staged.
Run relevant tests or checks before asking the skill to commit.
anti_patterns: Do not ask the skill to commit unrelated changes in one commit.
Do not bypass hooks unless the repository owner explicitly approves it.
Do not rely on generated messages without reviewing sensitive context.

faq.question: What commit style does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses the Conventional Commits format with type, optional scope, description, body, and footer.

faq.question: Can it stage files for me?
faq.answer: Yes. It can stage selected files, path patterns, or interactive hunks when you approve that workflow.

faq.question: Does it commit secrets?
faq.answer: It warns against committing .env files, credential files, and private keys. You should still review staged files.

faq.question: Can it create multi-line commit messages?
faq.answer: Yes. It can prepare a body and footer for commits that need more context.

faq.question: Will it rewrite existing commits?
faq.answer: No. The instructions tell it not to amend commits and not to run destructive Git commands without explicit approval.

faq.question: Which AI tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
